title: Kubernetes: from first object to platform reasoning
summary: 42 planned lessons teach observable reconciliation, workload networking, identity, state, release and recovery on host-owned disposable kind fixtures. No cluster or adapter is installed.
north_star: Declare an owned workload, prove desired state, ready traffic paths and data behavior, then diagnose and recover a bounded failure without touching another target.

stages.title: Build a reliable mental model
stages.outcome: Predict small examples, perform bounded changes and independently verify the first capstone.

stages.title: Compose and debug real systems
stages.outcome: Combine the mechanisms with explicit ownership, tests, failure cases and repeatable delivery.

stages.title: Defend engineering decisions
stages.outcome: Reason about concurrency or distributed control, measure tradeoffs and present a reviewed recovery/release capstone.

lessons.title: Terminal, files and an owned lab receipt
lessons.outcome: Identify the file being edited and the exact disposable target before any cluster action.
lessons.lab: Read an example host preparation receipt and trace command, context, namespace and output on a worksheet.
lessons.verification: Reject an expired or mismatched receipt and explain why an ambient current-context is never a course target.

lessons.title: Processes, containers, images and ports
lessons.outcome: Distinguish an image from a running process and a container port from a host port.
lessons.lab: Trace supplied offline container/network diagrams and an image-cache inventory.
lessons.verification: Correctly locate a process, an image digest and both sides of one port mapping; no engine installation is implied.

lessons.title: Kubernetes objects and YAML anatomy
lessons.outcome: Read apiVersion, kind, metadata and spec as an API request.
lessons.lab: Validate and apply a tiny namespaced fixture through the prepared worker credential.
lessons.verification: A deliberate indentation/type error is rejected; the accepted object's returned UID and namespace match the lease.

lessons.title: Identity, namespaces and explicit targeting
lessons.outcome: Demonstrate the difference between a namespace and permission to act in it.
lessons.lab: Use the private worker kubeconfig to create one allowed object and attempt a denied cluster action.
lessons.verification: The own-namespace action succeeds; namespace creation and cluster-role modification are forbidden; no credential is copied into progress.

lessons.title: Pods, image locality and logs
lessons.outcome: Explain Pod phase, container state and image availability separately.
lessons.lab: Run a preloaded nonroot HTTP fixture, inspect its logs and compare a host-provided missing-image negative case.
lessons.verification: The valid container starts offline; the negative case reports image absence without an automatic pull, and the learner distinguishes phase from readiness.

lessons.title: Deployments and reconciliation
lessons.outcome: Predict how a controller restores declared replica count.
lessons.lab: Create a two-replica Deployment and delete one owned Pod by recorded UID.
lessons.verification: A new Pod UID appears while Deployment UID stays fixed and observed generation/ready replica evidence converges.

lessons.title: Labels, selectors and Services
lessons.outcome: Connect a Service selector to a set of Pods rather than to an image name.
lessons.lab: Create an internal Service and compare matching and nonmatching label fixtures.
lessons.verification: The selector matches exactly the intended Pod UIDs and Service ports resolve to the documented container port.

lessons.title: Readiness and eligible Service backends
lessons.outcome: Diagnose why a running process can be ineligible for Service traffic.
lessons.lab: Complete the pilot: observe two ready backends, break a readiness path and repair a selector mismatch.
lessons.verification: Deployment/Pod state, ready EndpointSlice entries and an in-cluster HTTP client agree; port-forward alone is not accepted as routing proof.

lessons.title: ConfigMaps and configuration boundaries
lessons.outcome: Separate configuration data from the immutable image and observe when an application reloads it.
lessons.lab: Change a synthetic message through environment and mounted-file fixtures.
lessons.verification: The expected process sees the correct value; a snapshot records which update required a rollout and which required application reload support.

lessons.title: Requests, limits and namespace budgets
lessons.outcome: Distinguish scheduling requests, enforcement limits and quota admission.
lessons.lab: Compare a schedulable Pod with a quota-rejected and memory-limited fixture inside the lease.
lessons.verification: Events distinguish FailedScheduling, admission rejection and OOMKilled; the learner does not label all three as a readiness error.

lessons.title: Jobs and scheduled work
lessons.outcome: Choose a completion-oriented workload instead of an endlessly restarted service.
lessons.lab: Run a deterministic Job and inspect a preconfigured CronJob schedule/time-zone worksheet.
lessons.verification: Succeeded/failed counts and bounded retry/deadline behavior match the fixture; suspension prevents further scheduled runs before cleanup.

lessons.title: Debug from conditions, events and logs
lessons.outcome: Select evidence that distinguishes a configuration error from a runtime failure.
lessons.lab: Triage three offline/live paired fixtures: missing config, wrong probe and failed Job.
lessons.verification: Each diagnosis names a discriminating condition/event/log line and one minimal repair; unrelated resources remain unchanged.

lessons.title: Rollouts, revisions and recovery
lessons.outcome: Change declared state and verify rollout completion rather than trusting apply success.
lessons.lab: Roll a two-replica fixture between preloaded versions, introduce a bad readiness configuration and revert the manifest.
lessons.verification: Generation, updated/ready counts and response version agree after recovery; rollback evidence records the restored declarative file.

lessons.title: Capstone 1: observable stateless service
lessons.outcome: Deliver a small service and prove both convergence and reachability.
lessons.lab: Assemble Deployment, Service, ConfigMap and a bounded verifier Job, then repair one teacher-selected fault.
lessons.verification: Two eligible backends, correct HTTP payload, observed desired state and owner-scoped cleanup all pass from a fresh namespace.

lessons.title: Startup, liveness and readiness are different
lessons.outcome: Select a probe by the action Kubernetes should take after failure.
lessons.lab: Compare a slow-start fixture with a temporarily unready fixture and a permanently unhealthy fixture.
lessons.verification: Restart counts and endpoint readiness demonstrate the intended difference; thresholds are justified from fixture startup evidence.

lessons.title: Init containers and ephemeral shared files
lessons.outcome: Explain container ordering and the lifetime of emptyDir data.
lessons.lab: Use a finite init step and an application sharing a synthetic generated file.
lessons.verification: The application starts after initialization; container restart versus Pod replacement produces the documented file lifetime.

lessons.title: Nonroot workloads and Pod Security
lessons.outcome: Relate a security context to admission and actual process identity.
lessons.lab: Compare a restricted-compatible fixture with denied privilege/host-path variants supplied by the host.
lessons.verification: Allowed workload identity is nonroot; forbidden host namespaces, privileged mode and unapproved mounts fail before execution.

lessons.title: ServiceAccounts and RBAC boundaries
lessons.outcome: Prove a worker can perform its job without access to cluster administration.
lessons.lab: Inspect the provided Role/RoleBinding explanation and run positive/negative authorization checks.
lessons.verification: Own-object actions succeed while cross-namespace, Secret-reading and role-escalation actions are denied; workload tokens are not mounted by default.

lessons.title: Synthetic Secrets and reload semantics
lessons.outcome: Explain why base64 is encoding and why access paths matter more than a field name.
lessons.lab: Inspect offline fake-secret bytes and observe a host-provided synthetic Secret mount without collecting real credentials.
lessons.verification: Decoded dummy value is exact; the evidence names who can obtain it and distinguishes a mounted update from application reload.

lessons.title: DNS and layered network diagnosis
lessons.outcome: Separate DNS resolution, Service backend selection and application response.
lessons.lab: Use an in-cluster client to test a service name, a wrong port and an HTTP error endpoint.
lessons.verification: The report identifies which layer failed using DNS/result/backend evidence, with bounded timeouts and no external network dependency.

lessons.title: NetworkPolicy with enforcement evidence
lessons.outcome: Prove a policy changes permitted connectivity on a policy-capable fixture.
lessons.lab: In a dedicated policy-enabled lease, compare allowed and denied TCP client paths before and after default deny.
lessons.verification: The intended connection changes from success to bounded failure while the permitted path remains good; the lab is unavailable on an unqualified CNI.

lessons.title: Volumes, claims and stateful identity
lessons.outcome: Distinguish Pod replacement, persistent data and a storage class's guarantees.
lessons.lab: Use an owned synthetic PVC fixture and replace its application Pod without touching host personal directories.
lessons.verification: The expected marker survives Pod replacement; deletion/reclaim behavior is verified separately and is not called a backup.

lessons.title: Gateway, Ingress and the external route
lessons.outcome: Distinguish an internal Service from a host-facing HTTP route and the controller that implements it.
lessons.lab: In a dedicated lease with host-installed Gateway API/controller fixtures, attach an owned HTTPRoute and compare a matching route, an unmatched path and a synthetic TLS termination case; contrast an Ingress fixture.
lessons.verification: Gateway/Route Accepted and ResolvedRefs conditions plus the bounded client response agree; the host listener is loopback-only, the synthetic certificate is verified without bypassing TLS, and no external IP or controller installation is assumed.

lessons.title: Kustomize and field ownership
lessons.outcome: Review the full rendered resource before applying an overlay.
lessons.lab: Render dev/test overlays offline and inspect server-side apply ownership/conflict fixtures.
lessons.verification: Only declared fields differ, no namespace escapes appear and a field-manager conflict is explained instead of force-overwritten.

lessons.title: Helm values without hidden side effects
lessons.outcome: Treat a chart render as reviewable manifests rather than an opaque install.
lessons.lab: Render a pinned vendored chart offline; review values, hooks and cluster-scoped objects before namespaced apply.
lessons.verification: Rendered objects meet the allowlist; a fixture with a forbidden hook/CRD fails review without executing plugins or downloading a chart.

lessons.title: Placement and node-local DaemonSets
lessons.outcome: Compare a replica-count workload with one Pod per eligible node and explain affinity/taint constraints.
lessons.lab: Use host-supplied node facts to compare a Deployment with a restricted synthetic DaemonSet, then inspect affinity and taint/toleration negative fixtures without editing Nodes.
lessons.verification: DaemonSet desiredNumberScheduled and numberReady match qualified eligible-node facts; Pod placement or Pending events explain constraints, and the worker never patches shared Nodes.

lessons.title: Observability and service-level evidence
lessons.outcome: Define a meaningful availability/latency observation and connect it to a failure hypothesis.
lessons.lab: Collect bounded synthetic request results and, where provisioned, namespace metrics.
lessons.verification: Error counts and latency summaries match raw samples; missing metrics capability is reported explicitly and no monitoring stack is silently installed.

lessons.title: Capstone 2: stateful change with policy
lessons.outcome: Release and recover an owned stateful fixture with explicit access and data boundaries.
lessons.lab: Combine a small app, synthetic datastore, PVC, reviewed chart/overlay and policy-enabled clients.
lessons.verification: Connectivity, stored marker hashes, limited authorization and failed-change recovery all pass; cleanup respects the declared data retention choice.

lessons.title: Custom resources and structural schemas
lessons.outcome: Distinguish a custom resource instance from cluster-scoped API registration.
lessons.lab: In a dedicated advanced lease, request a reviewed host-provisioned CRD fixture and submit valid/invalid namespaced instances.
lessons.verification: Invalid fields are rejected by the schema; worker credentials cannot create arbitrary CRDs or widen their own privileges.

lessons.title: Operators and reconciliation contracts
lessons.outcome: Explain an operator's idempotent reconcile loop and status conditions without assuming Go knowledge.
lessons.lab: Drive a preloaded namespaced controller with repeated, changed and deleted custom resource fixtures.
lessons.verification: Observed resources and conditions converge without duplicate side effects; a supplied reconciliation trace explains requeue/finalizer behavior.

lessons.title: Admission policy and controlled denial
lessons.outcome: Separate API validation, authorization and admission decisions.
lessons.lab: Use a host-installed, lease-scoped policy fixture to deny an unsafe workload and allow its corrected form.
lessons.verification: The denial reason matches the policy, an allowed request succeeds and no arbitrary webhook endpoint or cluster-wide policy is installed by the worker.

lessons.title: Disruptions and availability budgets
lessons.outcome: Predict what an eviction budget protects and what it cannot prevent.
lessons.lab: Request an allowlisted drain of an owned worker node in an exclusive multi-node lease.
lessons.verification: Eviction behavior respects the PDB, readiness recovers and the learner distinguishes voluntary eviction from node loss.

lessons.title: Autoscaling with a qualified metrics path
lessons.outcome: Relate resource requests, measured load and stabilization to an HPA decision.
lessons.lab: Drive a bounded local load fixture against a host-provisioned metrics-enabled service.
lessons.verification: HPA status and replica movement fall within declared ranges and stabilize; no exact timing or production capacity claim is invented.

lessons.title: Traffic changes and progressive delivery
lessons.outcome: Design a release gate from application evidence instead of replica count alone.
lessons.lab: Compare rolling and two-version Service-selection fixtures with a synthetic failing release.
lessons.verification: Version/error samples meet the declared gate; a failed candidate is removed and finite samples are not claimed to prove an exact traffic ratio.

lessons.title: Watches and optimistic concurrency
lessons.outcome: Handle resource-version conflicts and watch expiration without losing state.
lessons.lab: Apply conditional edits to an owned object and replay a supplied expired-watch trace.
lessons.verification: One stale update receives409, relist/reconcile recovers and resourceVersion is not treated as a user-defined clock.

lessons.title: Control-plane snapshots and data backups
lessons.outcome: State what an etcd snapshot includes and which workload data it does not back up.
lessons.lab: In a dedicated synthetic cluster, request fixed host snapshot/restore operations and compare state with an independent PVC backup fixture.
lessons.verification: Restored API objects and application marker hashes are checked separately; private snapshot material is never exported as portable progress.

lessons.title: Version skew and replacement-cluster rehearsal
lessons.outcome: Test API compatibility across qualified versions without calling kind a production upgrade system.
lessons.lab: Render/validate fixtures against two separately owned pinned kind clusters and migrate only synthetic manifests/data.
lessons.verification: Compatibility differences are explained and the replacement cluster passes acceptance; no in-place production upgrade or HA proof is claimed.

lessons.title: Image provenance and offline verification
lessons.outcome: Distinguish content integrity from publisher provenance and policy enforcement.
lessons.lab: Evaluate prewarmed digest/signature-bundle fixtures with a qualified offline verification tool.
lessons.verification: Expected signed content is accepted, a tampered artifact is rejected and the report records trust inputs rather than equating a digest with authorship.

lessons.title: Multitenancy and threat boundaries
lessons.outcome: Explain why namespaces/RBAC alone are not an arbitrary-code isolation guarantee.
lessons.lab: Analyze adversarial supplied manifests and compare them with admission/runtime/network controls in an exclusive fixture.
lessons.verification: Each rejected behavior names its control; no learner can mount host paths, run privileged or obtain another lease's credentials.

lessons.title: Incident response and bounded fault injection
lessons.outcome: Choose a reversible investigation from a specific symptom and preserve evidence.
lessons.lab: Request one host-allowlisted synthetic fault, diagnose it and restore the last verified desired state.
lessons.verification: A timestamped evidence timeline distinguishes cause from symptom; unrelated namespaces and cluster settings are unchanged.

lessons.title: Recovery objectives and reviewable runbooks
lessons.outcome: Measure a recovery objective with both service and data evidence.
lessons.lab: Execute a documented synthetic recovery drill with explicit start/finish definitions and missing-step negative control.
lessons.verification: Observed recovery time and data-loss boundary are reported with source timestamps and marker hashes; a ready Pod alone is insufficient.

lessons.title: Capstone 3: platform release and incident review
lessons.outcome: Defend an end-to-end Kubernetes change and recovery story within a bounded owned environment.
lessons.lab: Release a policy-compliant custom-resource application, respond to a teacher-selected incident and perform a synthetic recovery drill.
lessons.verification: Application/data/authorization gates pass, every privileged operation has a dedicated lease receipt and cleanup removes only owned disposable resources.

capstones.title: Observable stateless service
capstones.brief: k8s-014 combines namespace-scoped workload, configuration and verification from a fresh lease.
deliverables: Minimal fault diagnosis and owner-scoped cleanup receipt
acceptance: Two eligible backend Pod UIDs agree with ready EndpointSlice entries.
An in-cluster client Job receives the expected payload.
A teacher-selected configuration fault is repaired and no outside resource is changed.

capstones.title: Stateful change with policy
capstones.brief: k8s-028 combines controlled configuration, synthetic persistent data and policy-capable networking.
deliverables: Reviewed vendored chart/overlay and resource inventory
Policy positive/negative tests and limited-identity evidence
acceptance: Data and service results survive the declared supported change.
Allowed/denied traffic proves actual CNI enforcement.
Failed change is recovered with explicit data retention and cleanup decisions.

capstones.title: Platform release and incident review
capstones.brief: k8s-042 uses an exclusive advanced lease for reviewed API/policy and recovery operations.
deliverables: Incident timeline and measured synthetic recovery drill
Privileged-operation lease receipts and final cleanup inventory
acceptance: Only the host provisioner performs reviewed cluster-level operations.
Recovery and cleanup prove the owned boundary; a kind lab is not presented as production HA acceptance.

pilot.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: echo
  labels:
    app: echo
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: echo
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: echo
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65532
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: echo
          image: ds60-http-fixture:v1
          imagePullPolicy: Never
          args: ["serve", "--port=8080"]
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 2
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 10m, memory: 16Mi}
            limits: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: echo
spec:
  selector:
    app: echo
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8080
      targetPort: http

concept.title: Running is not the same as ready for traffic
concept.explanation: The Deployment controller reconciles replica intent. A readiness probe controls whether a Pod is eligible for normal Service traffic. Service selectors and EndpointSlice ready conditions connect those separate mechanisms; apply success alone proves none of them.
concept.worked_example: Healthy replicas 2 yield two ready backend Pod UIDs. In a separate empty owned namespace, starting both replicas with probe /missing yields Running processes but zero eligible ready backends. A rolling change to an existing healthy Deployment can retain old Ready replicas and must be diagnosed by revision.

prediction.prompt: In the controlled all-unready fixture, no old Ready Pods match the Service. Both HTTP processes run, but both readiness probes return404. What should normal Service verification observe with publishNotReadyAddresses unset?
choices: Two healthy backends because Pod phase is Running.
Zero eligible ready backends; the containers need not restart.
prediction.explanation: A readiness failure removes normal traffic eligibility. EndpointSlice objects may still contain unready addresses, so count ready conditions rather than object existence.

hint_steps: Inspect desired replicas, Pod Ready conditions and Service selector separately.
Match ready EndpointSlice targetRef UIDs to Ready Pods; do not count all endpoints or use port-forward as a Service-routing proof.
Change one cause at a time, restore /ready and app:echo, then require both convergence and a successful in-cluster client Job before cleanup.
pilot.transfer_prompt: Design evidence for a second service named metrics whose Pods are Running but whose selector points at the wrong label, without changing the first service.
rubric: Predict the distinction between Running, Ready and eligible backend correctly.
Use only the explicit lease target and worker credential; never copy credentials into evidence.
Verify controller convergence, endpoint UID membership and in-cluster HTTP results independently.
Diagnose selector and readiness failures without confusing them with a container restart.
Clean up only owned resources and record that the runtime/fixture matrix is still pending.
